attempted_claim: Let Omega be a bounded Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain in C^n (n>=2) admitting a Lipschitz plurisubharmonic defining function in the sense of Michel-Shaw. For fixed 1<=q<=n let N_q be the L^2 d-bar-Neumann operator on (0,q)-forms. Is N_q compact iff the boundary contains no complex analytic variety of dimension >= q? In particular, does a 1-dimensional analytic disc in the boundary necessarily force noncompactness of N_1 in this rough class, or can N_1 remain compact?
decisive_failure: originality: Headline is substantively covered by prior Wang-Yuan-Zhang arXiv:2609.01561 Thm 1.1: same smooth complete Reinhardt Omega in C^3, same disc, same N1-compactness, same failure of P1/tilde-P1, with smooth psh defining function proved in Prop 2.3. Smooth on bounded closure implies Lipschitz, so Lipschitz-Michel-Shaw membership is a textbook one-line implication adding no new object, estimate, or boundary. Prior source need not state headline verbatim; its stronger smooth result implies the weaker Lipschitz corollary. This is repackaging of a known stronger fact, so originality FAILS.
